newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians in Israeli jails hold hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians in Israeli jails hold hunger strike.

text.p: Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails staged a one-day hunger strike on Wednesday to press for freedom and better conditions.
The protest was backed by a strike by Arab shopkeepers in East Jerusalem and a demonstration by families of some of the inmates in Gaza.

"All the Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails and detention camps have started a one-day hunger strike demanding their release and their full rights," said Hisham Abdel-Razek, Palestinian negotiator on the prisoners' issue.
"The hunger strike is a warning and it will be followed by other steps," he told reporters. He did not elaborate.

The Israeli Prisons Authority confirmed that the prisoners had refused to take food. "They refused the food three times today. They did this over an argument with the prisons authority over demanding improved conditions," a spokeswoman said.
Palestinians in Israeli jails have periodically gone on hunger strike to demand freedom and improved conditions.
Abdel-Razek said more than 3,500 Palestinians were in Israeli jails. Israeli officials put the figure at more than 2,000.
Abdel-Razek and 150 Palestinians, relatives of the prisoners, demonstrated in front of the Red Cross headquarters in Gaza in support of the inmates.
The crowd shouted: "We will not accept peace based on enlarging settlements and keeping prisoners hostage" and "We sacrifice our souls and blood for the prisoners."
In Arab East Jerusalem, Palestinian shops closed for the day in response to an appeal by the Palestinian Prisoners Committee (PPC).
A statement issued by the PPC said "the Palestinian prisoners are on a hunger strike to protest the highest degree of oppression by the Israeli authorities".

Interim peace deals signed by Israel and the PLO since 1993 include provisions for negotiations on a staged release of Palestinian prisoners. Abdel-Razek said talks on the issue "have achieved nothing yet".
